title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-12
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > Sonic Solutions > EAC > CoolEdit > CD

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of an incendiary Avalon 1968 set – smoking Dark Star, legendary Eleven and a blazing Other One suite.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers superb, almost studio‑quality sound for a 1968 show, preserving the band at a peak of psychedelic intensity. The performance is uniformly high‑energy with standout stretches of Dark Star, St. Stephen, Cryptical→The Other One and an unforgettable Eleven, plus a wild jam after New Potato Caboose. Minor mix quirks (loud shaker on Dark Star) are far outweighed by the overall clarity and power.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 80 reviews, all but one 5‑star; reviewers repeatedly praise both musical performance and audio fidelity. The few minor criticisms (shaker level, missing banter) are outweighed by the consensus of an exceptional show and excellent soundboard recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear, warm and detailed sound; some listeners note a slightly loud shaker on Dark Star and occasional mix imbalance, but overall the tape sounds like a modern master for a 1968 source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Seamless transitions – the Cryptical→Other One suite flows into New Potato, followed by a memorable drums‑jam‑feedback segment that ties the second set together.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is described as “ripping,” with soaring solos on Dark Star and powerful vocal delivery on Death Don't Have No Mercy.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass shines, especially on The Eleven (often called a ‘perfect’ or ‘thunderous’ performance).
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar and occasional vocals are noted; his singing on the Other One suite receives praise.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboards largely absent (no organ), which several reviewers comment on, but it does not detract from the overall impact.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart receive high marks for tight, driving drumming and the iconic drums‑jam‑feedback sequence.
